aspects.says: A case pattern doesn't narrow the type variable T, so a generic method can't return a typed value per case without unchecked casts; typed behaviour belongs in a method each record implements.
basis: section:A Sealed Interface of Records Brings Back an Exhaustive switch, but Not Typed Cases

aspects.says: An enum declaration can't take a type parameter (javac: 'enums cannot be generic'); JEP 301 proposed generic enums and was withdrawn, and erasure is not the reason.
basis: section:An Enum Can't Declare a Type Parameter; JEP 301 Proposed It and Was Withdrawn

aspects.says: The class writes values() and valueOf() itself: values() hands out a copy so callers can't change the registry, and valueOf throws IllegalArgumentException for an unknown name as Enum.valueOf does.
basis: section:The Registry Is Yours, and So Is Its Order

aspects.says: Constants of a class can't be case labels and can't key an EnumMap or EnumSet; a switch of guards needs a default and gets no coverage check.
basis: section:The Registry Is Yours, and So Is Its Order
aspects.reason: compile-time rules with no compiling wrong solution; the Reference table records them

aspects.says: Record constants are equal by value but not identical, so they are compared with equals, and a serialized record comes back as an equal copy.
basis: section:A Sealed Interface of Records Brings Back an Exhaustive switch, but Not Typed Cases
aspects.reason: record equality belongs to the records module (09-records); here it is one sentence of a trade-off, with nothing a test could grade beyond equals

aspects.says: Static initializers run in declaration order, so a registry declared after the constants is still null when their constructors add to it and the class fails to initialize.
basis: section:The Registry Is Yours, and So Is Its Order

aspects.says: Deserializing a constant of such a class creates a copy that is neither == nor equal to it, so map lookups miss; readResolve that returns the declared constant by name fixes both, while equals by name fixes only the lookup.
basis: section:The Class Must Rebuild values(), valueOf() and Serialization Itself
section:Spot the Problem: The Restored Config Runs on Defaults

aspects.says: A switch over a sealed interface of records with no default stops compiling when a record is added; a default branch silences that check.
basis: section:A Sealed Interface of Records Brings Back an Exhaustive switch, but Not Typed Cases

aspects.says: A final generic class with a private constructor and typed static final constants lets the compiler reject a value or a target of the wrong type for each key.
basis: section:A Final Class With Typed Constants Lets the Compiler Check Every Key
aspects.reason: the compiler enforces it, so no wrong solution compiles for a test to catch; the session-attributes practice is built on such a class
